statement: The printed global equality C:B=B*:C* is false for a nonreflexive order C, even in characteristic zero with separable fraction fields. Its height-one localization is valid; the refined statement is C-SA14-564.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: refuted literally by A=Q[x,y], B=Q(sqrt(2))[x,y], C=A+(x,y)sqrt(2); the conductor is (x,y)B while both trace duals equal B. C-SA14-564 gives the precise refinement.

statement: For every height-one prime p of the normal base, C*_p/C_p is isomorphic to C_p/D_p as a C_p-module if and only if the trace dual C* is invertible at all these localizations. Equivalently, C* is pseudo-invertible in the printed convention.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: both directions are established in the stated finite-order, separable-trace setting. The semilocal proof explicitly treats field and nonfield residue-algebra factors.

statement: The stated companion-series construction fails when the permitted nonnegative exponents include i=1,j=k=0. With positive exponents it has the block-recurrence proof recorded in C-SA14-565.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: literal range refuted under all printed hypotheses. Modulo x, the requested coefficient recurrence would make y^t divisible by every power of y. No such companion exists.

statement: For a one-dimensional Cohen–Macaulay local order C over a DVR with trace-dual canonical module ω and D=C:ω, the multiplier ring D:D equals C if and only if ω is invertible.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Complete local proof saved in proof_notes.md; regular parameter and locality are essential. The codimension-one global form follows by localization.

statement: If C is reflexive over the normal base A, then C:B=B*:C*. For every full order C, this equality and f_p C*_p=B*_p hold after localization at each height-one prime of A.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The global formula without C=C** is false; the corrected local formula is fully proved.

statement: With positive exponents i,j,k, ijk−ij−jk−ki≥0 and z^i∈Ax^j+Ay^k, the companion-series construction works. The literal allowance of zero exponents is false.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The general block recurrence is proved in proof_notes.md and checked for i=j=k=3 through27 coefficients. Zero-exponent counterexample is separate.

statement: With v=xy−z^(i−1)T and v′=Σ b_n x^(−n−1)T^n, the within-block exact recurrence is y b_(n+1)=z^(i−1)b_n. The printed division by x is inconsistent with this normalization; division by y is valid when the chosen powers of y make each coefficient integral.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Refuted even with positive coprime exponents in A=Q[x,y,z]/(z²−x⁵−y⁷), i=2,j=5,k=7. The proposed first coefficient has numerator y^t z(y−x) over x², whose numerator is nonzero modulo x. The refined recurrence is stated in this record.

statement: Let A be a complete noetherian local ring and f:X→Spec A a proper resolution, isomorphic over U=Spec A minus its closed point, with X regular and U schematically dense. Cartier divisors supported on X minus U give D→Pic(X)→Pic(U)→0; proper formal existence identifies Pic(X) with the compatible system of Pic(X_n). Only codimension-one exceptional components generate D; the blanket identification with every component of X_0 needs this qualification.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The divisor localization sequence is standard; formal existence is Grothendieck’s EGA III. The local-Picard application is developed explicitly by Lipman and Boutot. The two steps do not alone produce a representable quotient.

statement: For a non-separably-closed residue field, the exceptional divisor lattice is an étale Galois module obtained from the geometric exceptional components. Taking rational points of D→P→Q produces an H¹(k,im D) obstruction; replacing Pic(X_n) by its sheafified Picard functor adds a Brauer obstruction. Thus Q(k)=Pic(U) is not automatic. The text corrects the constant lattice to a twisted one.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Modern local Picard representability and Lipman’s exact sequence preserve the distinction between rational points of a Picard sheaf and actual line bundles. The source’s correction is essential; torsion-free constant lattices have H¹=0, whereas arbitrary twisted lattices need not.

statement: If a resolution admits an invertible ideal J defining the exceptional fibre set-theoretically and with ample conormal L=J/J² on Z, then the transition Pic(Z_{n+1})→Pic(Z_n) is eventually an isomorphism: H¹(Z,L^{n+1}) and H²(Z,L^{n+1}) vanish for large n. Hence its formal Picard pro-object stabilizes. The existence of such a J/model is a separate question in the source.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The conditional stabilization statement is established; the exact unrestricted model-existence assertion remains unverified in this bounded search.

statement: The map from exceptional divisors to NS of the special fibre is asserted to be injective, so that the divisor lattice embeds discretely and Pic(X)/D exists with the same connected component and Lie algebra. For normal surface singularities, negative definiteness of the exceptional intersection matrix proves the required injectivity. Higher dimensions require a negativity argument with precise projectivity hypotheses.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The normal surface case is classical and appears in the local-Picard literature. Kollár’s resolution description supports the quotient construction in his stated geometric setup. The exact generality of the handwritten expectation, especially without a projective birational model, was not established by the opened results.

statement: Under the stabilized-resolution construction, Lie(Q)=H¹(X,O_X) injects into H¹(U,O_U)=H²_m(A). Vanishing of this local cohomology, for example depth A≥3, makes Q discrete. An intrinsic functor on all k-algebras, independence of resolution, and behavior under non-geometrically-regular scalar extension are separately left open; a chosen coefficient field is part of the construction.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Boutot and subsequent local-Picard theory give an intrinsic functor in specified noetherian geometric settings. Kollár’s Condition 3 requires S₂, pure dimension at least3 and essential finite type over a field, and explicitly invokes Boutot’s representability theorem. These hypotheses cannot be discarded to claim representability for every complete local ring in the manuscript.

statement: For A an artinian local ring with perfect residue field k and X proper over A, seek a locally algebraic group over k representing the appropriate Picard functor formed through Witt-vector/Greenberg base change, including mixed characteristic; actual Pic(X) must be compared with its k-points through the descent obstruction.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Lipman’s 1976 paper explicitly identifies Grothendieck’s September1969 letter as the problem it answers. Definition1.1, Theorem1.2 and §5 construct the locally algebraic Picard group and reconcile the fpqc/fppf formulations; Theorem7.5 controls rational points. This is a precise later match, not merely a similar topic.

statement: For the normal affine cone over a smooth projective variety X with an ample embedding L and the usual section-ring hypotheses, the local Picard group at the vertex is Pic(X)/Z[L]. The blowup/line-bundle model and excision of the zero section give the quotient. Normality, generation and the distinction between the whole punctured cone and the punctured local spectrum are essential.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Kollár §25 gives the standard cone computation and compares local and completed local Picard groups. EGA II §8.7–8.8 gives the actual cone/contraction hypotheses; the manuscript’s norm argument supplies its own local-global comparison rather than making every graded ring a cone of this form.

statement: For a cone over a smooth projective curve C with polarization L, formal neighbourhoods of the exceptional curve have successive Picard kernels H¹(C,L^n), n≥1, because H²(C,L^n)=0. Over characteristic zero these give the unipotent correction to completion. For a smooth plane curve of degree d, the sum of these dimensions is binomial(d−1,3) for d≥4. The source’s d≥6 inequality is a sufficient example of failure of invariance, not the first possible degree.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The modern cone formulas in Kollár Example25 make the distinction between local and completed tangent spaces explicit. The finite positive-twist correction and the component quotient by the degree of L explain the curve case. Claims in higher dimension or positive characteristic need separate obstruction and group-structure analysis.

statement: For a noetherian henselian pair(A,J), restriction from U=Spec A minus V(J) to the corresponding puncture of the J-adic completion induces a bijection on Picard groups. This is an isomorphism on isomorphism classes, not automatically an equivalence of categories with all Hom groups preserved.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Elkik III.1 Theorem3 and the corollary on pp573–574 establish the vector-bundle/Picard comparison. No isolated-singularity condition is required in the cited corollary. This answers the source’s henselization hope with the noetherian henselian-pair hypotheses.

statement: For proper flat X/S with universal f_*O_X=O_S, the relative Picard functor is the fppf sheafification of T↦Pic(X_T)/Pic(T). A section g permits normalization L⊗f* (g*L)^{-1}, kills the Brauer obstruction and produces a rigidified description. Without a section, relative classes need not be represented by global line bundles. PicS→PicX→Pic_{X/S}(S)→H²(S,G_m) is the relevant low-degree exact sequence.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: FGA’s descent construction and Kleiman’s Comparison Theorem2.5 establish this distinction. It is invalid to identify the raw absolute Picard group with the sheaf of relative classes, or to omit the inverse in normalization. A Brauer–Severi family supplies the standard obstruction to a universal Poincaré bundle.

statement: Let X/S be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve and Y⊂X a finite étale divisor meeting every geometric fibre; set U=X∖Y and let E be the generalized Jacobian with torus Res_{Y/S}G_m/G_m. For n invertible on S, R¹f_!μ_n identifies with E[n] and R²f_!μ_n with Z/n, in the indicated relative convention. Nonempty punctures and invertibility of n are necessary.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The relative Kummer sequence and generalized Jacobian construction are established; Mazza–Voevodsky–Weibel §7 Proposition7.13 and Exercise7.14 give the relative-Picard calculation over a field. The relative family statement additionally uses proper/smooth base change and fibrewise comparison, with the source’s hypotheses retained.

statement: The low-degree compact-support Leray transgression defines ξ_n∈H²(S,E[n]); the page asks whether it equals the Kummer boundary of the degree-one Picard torsor of the curve with Y pinched. The equality, including its sign, is a question on the pages, not a completed calculation.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Harari–Szamuely Proposition2.2 identifies the fundamental-group extension class with the ℓ-adic boundary of the Albanese torsor over a field. Petrov–Skorobogatov2026 Theorem5.1 identifies the low Postnikov class for a torsor under a semiabelian variety with its Kummer boundary. These closely match the mechanism, but do not alone prove the exact relative compact-support/pinched-curve identity over arbitrary S.

statement: For proper flat finitely presented X/S with universally H⁰(O)=O_S, an abelian Picard identity component B, a Picard component P^δ and a local basepoint g, normalize the Poincaré bundle and take its determinant of cohomology M_g on P^δ. Relative perfectness (for example smooth or suitable lci proper data) is needed to define determinant pushforward functorially. Translation acts trivially on NS(P^δ), so the resulting class φ(δ) descends independently of g.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Knudsen–Mumford’s determinant functor gives the exact coherent-complex construction and base-change formalism; Mukai later develops the Fourier transform based on the same Poincaré kernel. A bare proper morphism does not automatically make every coherent pushforward perfect.

statement: Changing normalization from g to g′ twists the Poincaré family by the inverse of its evaluation at g′; its determinant changes by that line bundle to exponent−χ(δ). Consequently the associated map on the Albanese torsor changes by−χ times the difference of the two basepoints, for the standard determinant convention.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The determinant tensor rule and the theorem of the square establish the formula. Knudsen–Mumford supplies the canonical determinant construction; the sign follows from the inverse in normalization and is independently checked here, rather than read off an analogy with a theta divisor.

statement: Put Q=Alb¹(X), P=Pic_X^δ, R=Pic_B^{φ(δ)}, and define h(β)=t_β* M⊗M^{-1} for the determinant line M. With the positive Poincaré kernel and the standard determinant, the two equivariances are −χ on Q and +h on P. Thus the contracted A-torsor R+χQ−h_*P is trivialized by a coherently normalized determinant map. The manuscript instead writes R+χQ+tilde(φ(δ))_*P and explicitly requests a sign check; matching that display requires tilde(φ(δ))=−h or a correspondingly opposite kernel convention.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The determinant, Albanese and torsor ingredients are established in Knudsen–Mumford, Mukai and Alexeev. The exact three-torsor formula is not located verbatim as a named theorem in the searched sources. The modern signed relation follows conditionally from the explicitly fixed equivariance conventions, but the manuscript’s tilde/determinant dictionary and its claimed canonical trivialization are not certified by a torsor-class equality alone.

statement: Under Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch hypotheses, put a=Td(T_X)exp(δ), and let D=c₁(P) be the normalized Poincaré class. Then χ(δ)=∫_X a_n and c₁(det R p₂*(P⊗L))=(1/2)p₂*(a_{n−1}D²). With a perfect coefficient F, replace a bych(F)Td(T_X)exp(δ). This is the degree-two cohomological formula, not an assertion that all Chow components vanish.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The GRR formalism is developed in SGA6 and the Fourier calculus in Mukai/Beauville. The source’s coefficient and degree extraction are independently checked; the possible missing rank term a₀ on59:17 is recorded separately.

statement: For a smooth proper curve of genus g and a degree-d line bundle, χ=1−g+d. The associated NS class of det RΓ of the normalized Poincaré family is the negative of the canonical theta class for the standard determinant-of-cohomology convention. The source calls it the positive theta class while also flagging sign uncertainty; the discrepancy is conditional on determinant and translation conventions.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Mukai’s Fourier construction and the classical theta determinant description supply the established interpretation. Poonen–Stoll identifies the associated polarization torsor with Pic^{g−1}. The exact sign of Grothendieck’s symbol is left to the source convention, not silently rewritten.

statement: For a polarizationλ:A→A∨, the Poincaré pullback(1,λ)*P canonically represents2λ, with the usual rigidification. The source asks whether its independently constructed section of the doubled polarization torsor agrees with this canonical one. Existence of a section and equality of two canonical constructions are distinct questions.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Poonen–Stoll §4 and Alexeev Remark3.0.11 give the canonical doubled-polarization class. The source’s proposed comparison is not identified verbatim in the searched literature. It can only be claimed after comparing rigidifications and the translation/inversion conventions, not from2c_λ=0 alone.

statement: For the positive Poincaré Fourier transform, Φ(L⊗P_β)=t_β*Φ(L). If M=det Φ(L) and h_M(β)=t_β*M⊗M^{-1}, then l_g(λ+β)−l_g(λ)=+h_M(β). The support of t_β*D moves by−β, but this does not introduce a second minus into h_M, which already uses pullback. A formula with −tilde(φ(δ))(β) agrees when the tilde map is defined by image translation, equivalently by t_{−β}*; an inverse Poincaré kernel likewise changes the dictionary. The page twice asks to verify these signs.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Mukai §3, equation(3.1), gives the exact tensor/translation exchange. The modern statement is established after the kernel and pullback conventions are fixed. The source’s ambiguous sign and tilde convention remain a reading/formulation question; the manuscript’s exact signed three-torsor formula is separately retained in classC, C-SA14-657.

statement: For a smooth proper curve, the Albanese degree-one torsor identifies withPic¹ and its duality with the Jacobian is the canonical autoduality. Whether the manuscript’s mapc equalsλ_Θ or−λ_Θ depends on whether its Abel map isx↦O(x−x₀) orx↦O(x₀−x), and on translation conventions. The page’s proposed negative/symmetric sign is unfinished.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The canonical principal polarization and Pic^{g−1} theta torsor are established; Kleiman Remark5.26 explicitly uses the negative Abel conventionL⊗O(−Γ). Poonen–Stoll and Alexeev give the torsor form. These sources resolve the mathematics once the convention is fixed, but do not decide the ambiguous handwritten sign.

statement: A principally polarized abelian scheme(A,λ) canonically determines anA-torsorP together with a relative effective theta divisorΘ, unique up to the corresponding equivariant isomorphism. TakeP=Pic_A^λ with theA-action identified throughλ; the normalized Poincaré bundle has a rank-one section bundle and evaluation at0 definesΘ. For a Jacobian,P=Pic^{g−1}(C) andΘ=W_{g−1}.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Alexeev Construction3.0.5, Lemma3.0.6, Corollary3.0.7 and3.0.10 give precisely this construction and equivalence of groupoids. It does not require a global theta line bundle onA itself. Laga2025 shows that an unrestricted analogous assertion for every nonprincipal polarization is false in general.

statement: The inverse theta pair yields an involution on the theta torsor and a canonical section of its doubled contracted torsor. For a Jacobian this is L↦K_C⊗L^{-1} onPic^{g−1}, and the doubled section isK_C. The source’s final question asks comparison with the separate canonical section ofPic^{2λ}; that comparison still requires compatible rigidifications.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Serre duality/Riemann–Roch makes the Jacobian involution andK_C identification exact; Poonen–Stoll’s2-torsion class and Alexeev’s canonical doubled-polarization class are compatible endpoints. The last symbol-level identification is isolated as C-SA14-666 rather than declared proved merely because both classes exist.

statement: Construct a locally finite-type local Picard scheme without assuming that the punctured spectrum is regular, either by finding a proper modification on which all punctured line bundles extend or by descending line bundles from a resolution. Test whether H²_m(A)=0 implies that Pic(U) is countable and, over a separably closed coefficient field, invariant under separable extension after completed scalar extension.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Developed for the cited geometric hypotheses; no unrestricted complete-local-ring theorem or counterexample was established by the recorded search.

statement: Let f:X→S factor as X→Σ→S, with Σ→S finite and O_Σ→φ_*O_X an isomorphism preserved after every S-base change. Suppose g:Σ→X is a section of φ. Then Q(T)=Pic(X_T)/Pic(Σ_T) is the functor of g_T-rigidified line bundles up to isomorphism and is an fpqc sheaf. It identifies with the fppf-sheafified relative Picard functor of X/S, because line bundles on the finite scheme Σ_T become trivial Zariski locally on T. Flatness of Σ/S is not needed. The source’s successive Pic-prime and Pic-star conventions are preserved as historical stages, rather than identified without explanation.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The FGA descent/comparison framework establishes the rigidified Picard description. This more general finite-Stein-factor version is explicitly present on57:138–140 and is not reduced to the special case Σ=S. The normalization and sheaf-identification implications have also been independently re-proved in this run.
